insightScenarios.title: Explain Revenue Growth
insightScenarios.context: Revenue is up 12%, orders are up 4%, and average order value is up 7.7%.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write the manager-ready insight and one next action.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Revenue grew 12% while orders rose only 4%, with average order value up 7.7%, so most incremental growth appears to come from larger baskets rather than volume alone. Validate category mix and margin before shifting effort.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Retention Movement
insightScenarios.context: Month-3 retention improved from 62% to 71%, but the newer cohort is 40% smaller.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write a cautious retention insight and what should be checked next.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Month-3 retention improved from 62% to 71%, but the newer cohort is 40% smaller, so the improvement is encouraging but less precise. Compare cohort mix and segment retention, then monitor another cohort before changing the forecast.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Review Workload
insightScenarios.context: Online transactions are 2 of 7 observed transactions but both were review-flagged. Flags are routing signals, not confirmed fraud.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write a governance-safe insight for operations.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Online transactions are 2 of 7 observed transactions and both were review-flagged, which suggests concentrated review workload in this tiny sample but does not establish fraud. Validate the pattern on a larger sample before changing controls.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Capacity Pressure
insightScenarios.context: Saturday forecast arrivals exceed planned capacity by 25 while Friday exceeds by 15.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write an operational insight without making a clinical claim.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Saturday forecast demand exceeds planned capacity by 25 versus 15 on Friday, so Saturday has the larger operational gap. Run staffing and capacity scenarios and monitor wait and throughput; this is an operations signal, not a clinical conclusion.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Route SLA Risk
insightScenarios.context: NS-1 has 2 of 2 late shipments in the tiny sample, while NW-1 has 1 of 3.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write a decision-ready insight that avoids claiming the route code caused delay.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: NS-1 has 2 of 2 late shipments versus 1 of 3 on NW-1, so the observed late rate is higher on NS-1 but the sample is too small to claim the route caused delay. Expand the sample and compare carrier, distance and handoff conditions.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Refund Pressure
insightScenarios.context: Refund rate rose from 3.1% to 4.6% while order volume increased 18%. Electronics accounts for 52% of refund value.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write a manager-ready insight that separates overall growth from the refund problem and recommends one next analysis.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Refund rate rose from 3.1% to 4.6% while orders grew 18%, and electronics contributes 52% of refund value. Segment electronics by product, reason and supplier to determine whether growth mix or a specific quality issue is driving margin pressure.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Expansion Revenue
insightScenarios.context: NRR improved from 96% to 103%. Expansion MRR added ₹420k while churned MRR was ₹260k.
insightScenarios.prompt: Explain what moved NRR above 100% and what should be monitored before calling the improvement durable.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: NRR improved from 96% to 103% because ₹420k expansion MRR more than offset ₹260k churned MRR. Track expansion concentration and churn by segment over several periods before treating the improvement as durable.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Delinquency Mix
insightScenarios.context: Delinquent exposure is 6.8% overall but 11.2% in one small segment representing only 9% of total exposure.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write a governance-safe portfolio insight that avoids overreacting to a small segment.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Delinquent exposure is 6.8% overall and 11.2% in a segment that is only 9% of total exposure. The segment warrants review, but validate sample size, mix and underwriting characteristics before changing portfolio policy.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Wait-Time Change
insightScenarios.context: Median wait fell from 46 to 39 minutes, but the 90th percentile stayed at 88 minutes and Saturday demand remains above planned capacity.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write an operational insight that distinguishes typical experience from the long-tail problem.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Median wait improved from 46 to 39 minutes, but P90 remains 88 and Saturday demand is still above planned capacity. Typical experience improved while the long tail did not; segment high-wait periods and test capacity scenarios.

insightScenarios.title: Explain Cost per Shipment
insightScenarios.context: Average shipping cost rose 9%, but average shipment weight rose 14% and cost per kilogram fell 4%.
insightScenarios.prompt: Write a decision-ready cost insight and state which normalized metric should guide the next review.
insightScenarios.modelAnswer: Average shipping cost rose 9% while shipment weight rose 14%, and cost per kilogram fell 4%. The absolute cost increase appears partly volume/mix driven, so monitor normalized cost per kilogram and route mix before pursuing blanket cost cuts.

managerDialogues.title: Strong analyst communication
managerDialogues.message: You led with evidence, kept the claim bounded, recommended a concrete next step and connected it to business impact.

managerDialogues.title: Good direction
managerDialogues.message: The analysis is usable. Tighten the evidence or recommendation so a manager can act without filling in the gaps.

managerDialogues.title: Needs stronger evidence
managerDialogues.message: The direction may be reasonable, but the message needs clearer numbers, a bounded claim and an explicit next action.

managerDialogues.title: Rewrite before sending
managerDialogues.message: Start with the finding and evidence. Then add one recommendation and state why it matters to the business.

events.title: Dirty Vendor Data
events.context: A supplier sends a file with duplicates, mixed date formats and blank product codes 30 minutes before a weekly review.

choices.text: Validate grain, quarantine invalid rows, document the limitation and send a clean partial view if needed.
choices.feedback: Best choice. You protect decision quality without hiding the deadline.

choices.text: Delete every suspicious row quickly and present the remaining data as complete.
choices.feedback: Risky. Silent deletion can bias the result and hides uncertainty.

choices.text: Load the file unchanged because the meeting is urgent.
choices.feedback: Poor choice. Known quality problems should not be passed downstream without controls.

events.title: Urgent CEO Request
events.context: The CEO asks for an unfamiliar KPI in 20 minutes and wants one number for a board call.

choices.text: Confirm the metric definition, produce a clearly labeled preliminary estimate if feasible, and state assumptions.
choices.feedback: Best choice. Speed is balanced with definition and uncertainty.

choices.text: Guess the definition from a similar dashboard and send the number without caveats.
choices.feedback: Fast but unsafe. A wrong definition can create a confident wrong decision.

choices.text: Refuse to answer anything until a full multi-day analysis is complete.
choices.feedback: Overly rigid. A bounded preliminary answer can still be useful when labeled correctly.

events.title: Conflicting Reports
events.context: Finance reports ₹13.4M revenue while Sales reports ₹14.8M for the same month.

choices.text: Reconcile grain, status filters, date logic and metric definitions before choosing a source of truth.
choices.feedback: Best choice. Conflicting metrics are usually a definition or transformation problem to reconcile.

choices.text: Use the larger number because executives prefer growth.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Selecting a number for optics destroys metric integrity.

choices.text: Average the two reports and move on.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Averaging incompatible definitions produces a third unsupported number.

events.title: Privacy Incident
events.context: A shared analysis folder contains unnecessary personal identifiers that were not needed for the project.

choices.text: Stop further sharing, restrict access, follow the incident process and continue only with minimized fields.
choices.feedback: Best choice. Protect privacy, follow policy and minimize data.

choices.text: Ignore the extra fields because the analysis itself is correct.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Unnecessary exposure is a governance problem even if calculations are right.

choices.text: Copy the file to a personal device so it can be cleaned faster.
choices.feedback: Incorrect. Moving sensitive data to uncontrolled storage worsens the incident.
